home.featuresTitle: Everything your firm needs to move files forward
home.featuresSubtitle: Replace scattered spreadsheets, email threads, and ad-hoc portals with a practice system designed around immigration files.

projects.title: Immigration projects
projects.body: Open a file once: program, jurisdiction, status, and participants. Forms and document checklists seed from a standard pathway or a template your firm maintains.

people.title: Lifelong client records
people.body: Keep clients as durable records across engagements — contact details, consultation notes, immigration status, and expiry dates in one place.

forms.title: Ask-once questionnaires
forms.body: Clients answer once. Your team uses those answers to prepare IRCC PDFs, including IMM 5476 representative details from the assigned staff profile.

documents.title: Document collection and review
documents.body: Ask for passports, photos, and custom files. Clients upload in the portal; your firm previews, approves, or sends a file back with a comment.

contracts.title: Document templates and signing
contracts.body: Write or upload retainers in each language you serve, insert booking details automatically, and send them for electronic signature when a client books. Clients type or draw a mark; you can countersign or pre-sign.

share.title: Client portal
share.body: Invite clients to a lasting portal. They sign in with the email on their file and a password handled on the server — never in the browser. Documents, questionnaires, invoices, and appointments stay in one place.

booking.title: Google Calendar and Google Meet
booking.body: Each consultant connects their own Google Calendar. Public booking skips busy times, confirmed appointments sync to the calendar, and a Google Meet link is attached for the call.

payments.title: Square or Stripe payments
payments.body: Connect Square or Stripe to collect consultation fees at booking or send a payment link on a file — one processor per firm. Clients pay on that checkout. Unpaid bookings surface on the home screen.

sage.title: Sage Accounting
sage.body: Match clients to Sage by email, apply the correct provincial sales tax, and post invoices when Square or Stripe payments complete.

team.title: Firm workspace
team.body: Each consulting firm is its own tenant. Invite admins and case managers. Work in English, French, or Spanish — including the client-facing flows they use.

one.title: Create the project
one.body: Add participants inline, pick the program or a firm template, and seed the forms and document checklist in one screen.

two.title: Collect once
two.body: Invite clients to the portal so they upload documents and complete the questionnaire. Review uploads without chasing email attachments.

three.title: Book, meet, and get paid
three.body: Clients book on your public page. Calendar blocks busy time, a meeting link is attached, Square or Stripe collects the fee, and a contract can go out for signature.

four.title: Prepare and close
four.body: Fill IRCC PDFs from answers already collected, keep signed contracts with the file, and retain or destroy closed files to match your firm’s duties.

preview.serviceConsultDesc: First meeting to review your situation

integrations.title: Booking and contracts included — then the tools you already use
integrations.subtitle: A public booking page and electronic signature ship with the product, and they share data. You don’t need a separate scheduler, a signing product, or a connector between them. Then connect the calendar, meetings, payments, and accounting you already run.

builtin.title: Included in the product
builtin.help: Weekly open hours, a public booking page, retainer templates, and e-signature. When a client books, the contract can fill from that appointment and go out to sign.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.help: Connect one calendar. Public booking skips busy times; confirmed appointments are written there.

meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.help: Choose one meeting tool for join links on confirmed bookings.

payment.title: Payments and accounting
payment.help: Connect Square or Stripe — one processor per firm. Collect consultation fees at booking or send a payment link on a file. Connect Sage to post matching tax invoices.

booking.title: Public booking
booking.body: Share a booking page with your weekly open hours and paid services. Prospective clients pick a time, pay, and get a confirmation. Busy times on a connected calendar are skipped automatically.

contracts.title: Contracts and e-signature
contracts.body: Write or upload templates in each language you serve. Booking details fill in automatically — name, service, date, meeting link. Send for signature when they book. Clients type or draw a mark; you can countersign or pre-sign.

calendar.title: Google Calendar
calendar.body: Each staff member connects their Google Calendar in calendar settings. Public booking and call invites respect busy times and blocked hours. Confirmed appointments are created on that calendar.

outlook.title: Outlook Calendar
outlook.body: Connect Microsoft 365 Outlook instead of Google. Public booking respects Outlook busy times, and confirmed appointments are created on that calendar.

meet.title: Google Meet
meet.body: When a calendar is connected, each confirmed booking can include a Google Meet link. Clients join from the confirmation page, the email, or the manage-booking link.

teams.title: Microsoft Teams
teams.body: Each confirmed booking can include a Microsoft Teams join link. Clients join from the confirmation page, the email, or the manage-booking link. Works with Google Calendar or Outlook.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.body: Each confirmed booking can include a Zoom Meeting link. Clients join from the confirmation page, the email, or the manage-booking link. Works with Google Calendar or Outlook.

square.title: Square
square.body: Connect Square to charge consultation services and send payment links on a project. Clients check out on Square. You see unpaid bookings on home until they pay.

stripe.title: Stripe
stripe.body: Connect Stripe to charge consultation services and send payment links on a project. Clients check out on Stripe. You see unpaid bookings on home until they pay. There is no platform cut.

sage.title: Sage Accounting
sage.body: Connect Sage Business Cloud Accounting to match clients by email, apply the right Canadian sales tax, and post invoices when Square or Stripe payments complete.

home.securityTitle: No AI. Passport scans stay in your practice.
home.securitySubtitle: Nobody wants a passport scan to land in another country’s AI datacenter. %PRODUCT_NAME% does not use any AI service. We treat your data with automation workflows and logic gates — rules your firm controls — not models trained on client files.

noAi.title: No AI in the pipeline
noAi.body: Questionnaires, PDF fill, booking, and document review run on software logic. We do not send client files to generative AI providers.

canada.title: Primary data in Canada
canada.body: Database, authentication, and file storage run on Supabase in Canada (AWS Canada Central).

encryption.title: Encryption that matches the risk
encryption.body: TLS in transit, infrastructure encryption at rest, and firm-level AES-256-GCM for uploaded documents and many identity fields.

access.title: Your firm’s data stays yours
access.body: Access is scoped to each organization. Public booking pages use unguessable tokens with rate limits and expiry where configured.

privacy.title: Privacy you can explain
privacy.body: Written to support PIPEDA accountability, with closed-file retention tools aligned to typical CICC six-year duties — not a certification, and not legal advice.

audience.a: Yes. It is practice software for Canadian immigration consultants and lawyers — clients, IRCC forms, booking, and payments in one workspace.

ai.q: Does %PRODUCT_NAME% use AI with client files?
ai.a: No. Questionnaires, PDF fill, booking, and document review run on software logic. We do not send client files to generative AI providers.

data.a: Database, authentication, and file storage run on Supabase in Canada (AWS Canada Central).

trial.a: Standard is free for 30 days from when you create your firm. No credit card is required.

languages.q: Can my firm work in French or Spanish?
languages.a: Yes. Staff and client-facing flows work in English, French, and Spanish.

home.finalSubtitle: Set up your firm workspace in minutes and see whether it fits how you already practice.
home.finalNote: The full product from the day you create your firm. No credit card.

trial.a: No. The product is free for {days} days from when you create your firm, with no credit card. We email firm administrators before billing starts.

docs.title: Integration documentation
docs.intro: This page explains how to add, use, and remove connected apps in %PRODUCT_NAME%. Zoom is documented in full below — it is the meeting-link app listed on the Zoom Marketplace.
docs.zoomIntro: %PRODUCT_NAME% can create a Zoom Meeting for each confirmed public booking and put the join link on the confirmation screen, emails, and the link clients use to change or cancel the appointment. Zoom is the meeting tool. A calendar (Google Calendar or Outlook) is still what blocks busy times.
docs.addIntro: Each staff member connects their own Zoom account.

addSteps.four: Sign in to Zoom and allow the requested permissions (create, update, and delete meetings, and read your Zoom user profile).
addSteps.five: You return to Calendar settings. Zoom is connected and selected for booking join links.

docs.addPrereqBody: A %PRODUCT_NAME% staff account in a firm workspace, and a Zoom account that can host meetings. If your Zoom admin restricts Marketplace apps, they must allow %PRODUCT_NAME%.
docs.usageIntro: The Zoom app does one job: meeting join links on bookings.
docs.usageFeatureBody: When a client books a consultation on your public booking page, %PRODUCT_NAME% creates a Zoom Meeting on the connected account (title and start/end time) and stores the join URL on the booking. Clients open that link from the confirmation, email, or manage-booking page. If the booking is rescheduled, %PRODUCT_NAME% updates the Zoom Meeting. If the booking is cancelled or deleted while Zoom is still connected, %PRODUCT_NAME% tries to delete that meeting.
docs.usagePrereqBody: Zoom connected and in use under Settings → Account → Meetings. Public booking turned on for that staff member. A calendar connected (Google Calendar or Outlook) so available slots can be offered — Zoom does not sync your calendar busy times.
docs.removeIntro: You can disconnect %PRODUCT_NAME% from Zoom in either product. Do both if you want access fully revoked and tokens deleted on our side.

removeDossierlySteps.three: Under Meetings, on Zoom, select Disconnect.

docs.removeDossierlyBody: That deletes your Zoom connection and encrypted OAuth tokens from %PRODUCT_NAME%. New bookings will not get a Zoom link. %PRODUCT_NAME% will not create, update, or delete meetings on your Zoom account after that.

removeZoomSteps.two: Open the Zoom App Marketplace, then Manage → Installed Apps, or go to marketplace.zoom.us/user/installed.

docs.removeDeauthBody:
Removing the app in Zoom revokes %PRODUCT_NAME%’s access to your Zoom account. We can no longer create, update, or delete meetings. Existing Zoom meetings already created stay on your Zoom account until you delete them in Zoom. Booking records in %PRODUCT_NAME% (including a stored join URL) stay with the firm’s file under our Privacy Policy — disconnecting Zoom does not erase client bookings. Join links already sent to clients keep working on Zoom until those meetings are deleted there.

After you remove the app in Zoom, also select Disconnect in %PRODUCT_NAME% Settings → Account so we delete stored tokens immediately. Copies of meetings on Zoom, emails already sent, and backups can outlive the disconnect until those copies expire.
docs.troubleshootingBody:
Access was not granted: connect again and approve every permission Zoom shows.

Reconnect required, or the connection failed: select Disconnect, then Connect Zoom again.

Zoom did not return a refresh token: revoke %PRODUCT_NAME% in your Zoom Installed Apps list, then connect again from %PRODUCT_NAME%.

Bookings have no Zoom link: confirm Zoom shows as in use under Meetings, public booking is on, and a calendar is connected.
docs.otherBody: Google Calendar, Google Meet, Outlook, and Teams are connected from the same Settings → Account screen. Calendar tools sync busy times and write the appointment; meeting tools supply the join link. You may use Zoom with Google Calendar or Outlook.

legal.privacyIntro:
%PRODUCT_NAME% is practice-management software operated by %OPERATOR_AS% for Canadian immigration consultants. This policy describes how personal information is collected, used, disclosed, and protected when you use %PRODUCT_NAME% — including the consultant workspace, the client portal, and public booking pages. Use of the service is also governed by our Terms and Conditions.

This policy supports accountability under the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) and Québec’s Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25). It is not a certification, not legal advice, and not a retainer with %OPERATOR_NAME% for immigration services.

Primary records are stored in Canada. Uploaded files and many identity fields are encrypted. The firm’s staff can open the file in their workspace. %OPERATOR_AS% processes it to operate the platform, including with vendors that may be outside Québec, as described in the Privacy Policy. Optional analytics are off unless you accept them.

controller.title: 1. Who is responsible
controller.body:
Your consulting firm (the organization with a %PRODUCT_NAME% workspace) decides why and how client personal information is processed for its immigration services. That firm is the organization responsible for the client file.

%OPERATOR_NAME% operates the software and processes client and booking-guest information on the firm’s instructions as a service provider. %OPERATOR_NAME% is responsible for staff-account information it uses to run the service (name, email, authentication identifiers, and similar operational data).

If you book an appointment or complete a form through a firm’s link, you are giving information to that firm. %OPERATOR_NAME% hosts and processes it so the firm can use the software. Questions about immigration advice, retainers, fees, or how the firm uses your file should go to the firm — not to %OPERATOR_NAME% as your representative.

officer.title: 2. Privacy officer
officer.body:
The person in charge of the protection of personal information at %OPERATOR_NAME% is Adrien Yvin, Privacy Officer, %PRIVACY_EMAIL%.

That contact is published as required by Québec Law 25. You may write to the same address for PIPEDA inquiries about the platform. If you are a client of a consulting firm, contact that firm first about your immigration file.

purposes.title: 3. Purposes
purposes.body:
We process personal information to:
• Provide the CRM, questionnaires, form preparation, document intake, client portal, calendar, and public booking features
• Authenticate staff and, where a firm enables it, client portal access
• Send appointment confirmations, change/cancel links, and reminder emails the firm configures
• Sync busy times and bookings with a consultant’s Google Calendar or Outlook calendar when that consultant connects it, and create a Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Zoom join link when that meeting tool is selected
• Maintain security, prevent booking abuse, keep audit records, and operate the service
• Collect consultation fees through Square or Stripe when the firm connects a payment processor, and post matching tax invoices to Sage when the firm connects Sage Accounting
• Bill the firm for the software through Stripe when a paid plan applies
• Meet legal obligations that apply to %OPERATOR_NAME% as a service provider and as an enterprise

We do not sell personal information. We do not use client file contents for advertising. We do not use personal information for new purposes without notice and, where the law requires, a new consent.

collection.title: 4. What we collect
collection.body:
Depending on how the product is used, this may include:

Staff and firm: name, email, role, representative profile fields used on IMM 5476, authentication identifiers, the firm’s default language, and — if a consultant connects Google Calendar, Outlook, Google Meet, Teams, or Zoom — that connected account’s email.

Clients and booking guests: first name, last name, email, phone, address (when asked at booking), preferred language, immigration-status fields a firm records, questionnaire answers, extra questions a firm adds to a booking form, uploaded supporting documents (for example a passport), consultation notes, and generated form files. Immigration files often include sensitive information and may include information about family members, including minors.

Bookings: appointment time, service, consultant, when privacy notice was accepted, meeting join links when created, Zoom or Teams meeting identifiers, and hashed email and IP used only to rate-limit the public booking page.

Calendar and meetings (only if a consultant connects them): encrypted OAuth tokens; the connected account email; busy intervals and event titles from Google Calendar or Outlook; and meeting join URLs. New bookings are written to the connected calendar with the guest’s name, email, and phone in the event details. If Zoom is the meeting tool, we create a Zoom meeting on that consultant’s Zoom account with the appointment title and time, then store the meeting id and join URL. We do not send the guest’s email to Zoom as a registrant, do not access Zoom cloud recordings, chat, or phone, and do not use Zoom data for advertising.

Payments (only if the firm connects Square or Stripe): checkout identifiers, amount, status, and the guest or client contact details needed to create the charge.

Accounting (only if the firm connects Sage): client name, email, billing address, and invoice amounts posted to the firm’s Sage business.

Technical: security audit events (including IP address and browser user-agent for some actions), hashed IP and email for booking abuse control (about 14 days), and — only if you opt in — product usage and performance metrics.

Firms should collect only what they need for the engagement. Extra booking questions are stored with the appointment. We do not operate a biometric identification system.

legalBasis.title: 5. Consent and notice
legalBasis.body:
Firms are responsible for obtaining valid consent from clients where required — including express consent for sensitive information and, in Québec, parental or guardian authorization before collecting information about a child under 14 — and for explaining their own retainers and privacy practices.

Staff must accept this Privacy Policy and the Terms and Conditions when they create a %PRODUCT_NAME% account. The client portal requires both checkboxes when the client first creates a password or first signs in with Google. Public booking requires both checkboxes before a booking can be submitted. Checking those boxes is consent to the processing described here for that account, file, or appointment, subject to the firm’s instructions and applicable law. Those checkboxes are not pre-checked.

Calendar, meeting, payment, and accounting tools are off until a staff member or the firm connects them. Connecting them is an instruction to communicate related details to that provider. Optional product analytics are off until you accept them in the cookie banner.

You may refuse by not creating an account, not using the link, or not booking. You may ask the firm to withdraw consent or delete information, subject to professional retention rules. Some processing (security logs and legal retention) may continue where the law allows.

governance.title: 6. Governance
governance.body:
%OPERATOR_NAME% maintains policies on collection, use, access, retention, destruction, confidentiality incidents, and vendors. A plain-language summary and related templates can be downloaded from this page and from Settings → Security in a firm workspace.

Consulting firms remain responsible for their own governance toward their clients, including a privacy impact assessment when Québec Law 25 requires one.

safeguards.title: 7. Safeguards
safeguards.body:
We apply safeguards proportionate to the sensitivity of immigration files, including:
• Encryption in transit (TLS)
• Infrastructure encryption at rest for the database, authentication, and file storage
• Application-level AES-256-GCM for uploaded client documents and for many client fields (names, emails, phones, notes, questionnaire answers, booking guest details, and similar), using a separate encryption key per firm
• Some operational fields are stored without that application-level encryption (for example preferred language, immigration-status labels, appointment times, and security audit metadata)
• Access controls scoped to each firm; Admin and Case Manager roles control who can administer the workspace versus work the caseload
• Database service-role privileges restricted to server-only paths
• Public booking pages identified by unguessable tokens; booking rate limits use hashed email and IP
• Staff passwords handled by Supabase Auth; client portal passwords stored in a private schema and verified only on the server; optional Google sign-in for the client portal is verified on the server and does not create a staff account

Yuzu personnel who hold the platform wrap key can technically decrypt firm keys in order to operate, restore, or secure the service, or to comply with law. We limit that access operationally. No method of transmission or storage is perfectly secure. You use the service understanding that residual risk.

retention.title: 8. Retention and destruction
retention.body:
Client and project records remain while the firm’s workspace is active. When a file is closed, the product sets a retain-until date of six years after closure to support typical College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants closed-file duties. That professional retention is a documented purpose. A client may ask the firm to delete their information (including from the client portal Security page). The firm generally cannot destroy a closed file until those six years have passed. When purposes are fulfilled, Québec Law 25 requires destruction or anonymization.

Deleting a client or a project from the workspace erases that record’s personal information in the application: identity and contact fields, notes, uploaded documents, questionnaire answers, portal access, and linked bookings (including an attempt to delete the matching Google Calendar or Outlook event and any Zoom or Teams meeting created for it). Disconnecting Zoom from Settings deletes that staff member’s Zoom OAuth tokens from %PRODUCT_NAME%. People who remain on another file at the firm are kept. After the retain-until date, a firm administrator can destroy a closed file the same way. A placeholder project row and an encrypted destruction-register entry (client name and service summary) are kept for the firm’s professional record. Security audit rows for that file or person are kept as a record that the action occurred, with IP address, user agent, and event metadata removed.

Hashed booking abuse events are deleted after about 14 days, and are also removed for an erased person’s email.

Emails already sent, copies of calendar events or meetings held by Google, Microsoft, or Zoom, payment records at Square or Stripe, invoices at Sage, and database backups or point-in-time recovery copies can outlive an application delete until those copies expire. Firms remain responsible for their professional retention and secure-destruction duties.

sharing.title: 9. Sharing and service providers
sharing.body:
We use these providers to run %PRODUCT_NAME%:
• Supabase (Canada) — database, authentication, and file storage
• Vercel — application hosting, logs, and optional Web Analytics and Speed Insights
• Resend — transactional email when mail sending is configured (confirmations, reminders, and manage links)
• Stripe — billing for the firm’s %PRODUCT_NAME% subscription when a paid plan applies; consultation payments only if the firm connects Stripe
• Google — only if a staff member uses Google to sign in, a firm enables Google sign-in on the client portal, or a consultant connects Google Calendar or Google Meet
• Microsoft — only if a consultant connects Outlook Calendar or Microsoft Teams
• Zoom — only if a consultant connects Zoom
• Square — only if the firm connects Square for priced bookings
• Sage Business Cloud Accounting — only if the firm connects Sage to match clients by email and post tax invoices

A current list is available for download from this page. Those providers process the information we send them to provide their service. We do not disclose client file contents to third parties for their marketing. We may disclose information if required by law, to protect rights and security, or on the firm’s instructions (for example sending a reminder the firm wrote).

When a consultant connects a calendar, that provider receives the booking details the product writes there (including guest name, email, and phone), and we receive busy times and event titles from that calendar. When Zoom is connected, Zoom receives the meeting title and start/end time on that consultant’s Zoom account and returns a join URL. When Square or Stripe is connected for consultation fees, that processor receives the amount and the payer’s contact details needed to complete checkout. When Sage is connected, Sage receives the client’s name, email, billing address, and invoice amounts for the firm’s own accounting.

transfers.title: 10. Location of processing
transfers.body:
Primary application data (database, authentication, and stored files) is hosted in Canada (AWS Canada Central — Montréal — via Supabase).

The application is hosted on Vercel. Compute and logs may be processed outside Canada, including the United States. Optional analytics, if you accept them, may also be processed there.

Transactional email via Resend, Stripe billing, and Google, Microsoft, Zoom, Square, Stripe Connect, or Sage when a staff member or the firm connects those services, are processed by those providers outside Canada, including the United States (and, for Sage, typically the United Kingdom).

If you are in Québec, some personal information may therefore be communicated outside Québec. %OPERATOR_NAME% has assessed those communications under Law 25. Firms that enable a calendar, meeting, payment, or accounting tool instruct us to send the related information to that provider and remain responsible for their own transfer assessments where the law requires them.

cookies.title: 11. Cookies and usage data
cookies.body:
Essential cookies store a signed-in session (staff or client portal) and a few interface preferences, such as whether the sidebar is collapsed. The language of the page comes from the URL. Those cookies are necessary to operate the service.

Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights are optional. They collect page-view and performance data to help us operate the product. They are not used to sell advertising. They are off until you accept them in the banner. You may refuse. Highest-confidentiality parameters are the default: analytics stay off unless you opt in.

rights.title: 12. Your rights
rights.body:
Subject to PIPEDA, Québec Law 25, and other applicable law, individuals may request access to, correction of, deletion of, a portable copy of computerized personal information (in a structured, commonly used technological format), or information about the handling of their personal information. We aim to respond within 30 days.

Clients who use the client portal can open Security in that portal. There they can download a copy of their personal information and the information of other people on immigration files they belong to, and they can send a deletion request to the firm’s legal or security contact. That request is not an immediate erase: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants rules require a closed client file to be kept for six years after the file is closed. Until that hold ends, the firm generally cannot destroy the file. After that, a firm administrator can destroy it as described in section 8.

Clients and booking guests may also contact the consulting firm directly. Guests can use the change or cancel links in their confirmation email while those links are valid. Firm administrators may use in-product export tools (person JSON export and project file ZIP) and, where professional retention allows, delete a person or destroy a closed file.

You may also contact %OPERATOR_NAME% using the details below. You may complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, and in Québec to the Commission d’accès à l’information.

breach.title: 13. Confidentiality incidents
breach.body:
%OPERATOR_NAME% keeps a register of confidentiality incidents. If we become aware of an incident, we assess whether it creates a risk of serious injury (Québec) or a real risk of significant harm (PIPEDA).

Where the law requires, we will notify the Commission d’accès à l’information and/or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, notify affected firms, and give firms the facts they need to notify their clients. We will notify individuals directly when we are the organization responsible for that information or when a firm cannot reasonably do so.

This is not a waiver of any defence. Notification is made because the law requires it when the threshold is met.

children.title: 14. Children and dependents
children.body: The service may store information about minors when they are part of an immigration file. Firms must ensure collection is necessary and, in Québec, generally authorized by a parent or guardian if the child is under 14, or as otherwise permitted by law. %OPERATOR_NAME% does not knowingly collect children’s information except as a service provider on a firm’s instructions.

automated.title: 15. Automated decisions
automated.body: %PRODUCT_NAME% does not make a decision based exclusively on automated processing of personal information that produces legal effects or similarly significant effects concerning a person. Form fill is a drafting aid. Licensed staff must review every form and filing. If that changes, we will say so in this policy and offer the information the law requires.

changes.title: 16. Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy to reflect product, legal, or security changes. The “Last updated” date will change when we do. Material changes will be highlighted in-product or by notice to firm administrators when practical. Where the law requires a new consent, we will ask for it.

If you are a client of a consulting firm, contact that firm for requests about your immigration file or booking. Templates for firms are available for download on this page.

agreement.title: 1. Agreement
agreement.body:
By creating an account, joining a firm workspace, signing in to the client portal, or submitting a public booking, you agree to these Terms and Conditions and to the Privacy Policy.

If you do not agree, do not use %PRODUCT_NAME%. If you accept on behalf of a consulting firm, you confirm that you have authority to bind that firm. These terms are a contract of adhesion for some users; we have tried to write them in clear language. External documents (including the Privacy Policy and the Firm Data Processing Addendum) are brought to your attention by these terms and by in-product links and checkboxes. A firm administrator accepts the addendum when creating the workspace, or later in Settings. That clickwrap is the written processor contract. A countersigned copy is optional.

parties.title: 2. Who these terms apply to
parties.body:
%OPERATOR_NAME% operates %PRODUCT_NAME%.

A “firm” is the consulting organization that holds a workspace. “Staff” are the firm’s users (owner, admins, and case managers).

A “client” or “guest” is someone who uses a firm’s client portal or public booking page. Clients have a relationship with the firm, not a professional retainer with %OPERATOR_NAME%

Sections that impose professional, indemnity, or payment duties on a “firm” apply to firms and staff acting for them. They do not impose those duties on clients or guests, except the acceptable-use and accuracy rules that apply to everyone.

service.title: 3. The service
service.body:
%PRODUCT_NAME% is software for practice management: client records, questionnaires, form preparation, document intake, client portal, calendar, public booking, contracts and e-signature, consultation payments, and optional accounting.

Staff may connect Google Calendar or Outlook, and Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Zoom for meeting join links. A firm may connect Square or Stripe to collect consultation fees, Sage Business Cloud Accounting to post tax invoices, and Google sign-in for staff and, if the firm enables it, the client portal. %OPERATOR_NAME% bills the firm for the software through Stripe when a paid plan applies. Transactional email, when configured, is sent through Resend. Application hosting is on Vercel; the system of record is Supabase in Canada.

%OPERATOR_NAME% provides the software. Features may change. We may add, change, or remove functions with reasonable notice when practical. We do not warrant that a particular form edition, government portal, or third-party API will remain available.

noProfessionalRelationship.title: 4. No immigration advice or professional relationship
noProfessionalRelationship.body:
%OPERATOR_NAME% does not provide immigration advice, representation, or legal services. It is not a member of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants and is not a law firm. It is not affiliated with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) or the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l’Intégration (MIFI).

Nothing in the software, generated forms, emails, or these terms creates a consultant–client, lawyer–client, or fiduciary relationship with %OPERATOR_NAME% Staff must review every form and filing before it is used. %OPERATOR_NAME% does not warrant immigration outcomes or that a government authority will accept a generated form.

Clients and guests look only to the firm for professional services. Any claim arising from advice, filings, delays, refusals, or fees is a matter between the client and the firm, except to the extent a mandatory law makes %OPERATOR_NAME% responsible for its own acts as a software provider.

accounts.title: 5. Accounts and credentials
accounts.body:
Staff accounts are for people authorized by a firm. You must provide accurate information, keep credentials confidential, and tell the firm promptly if you lose access. The firm is responsible for who it invites and which role it assigns. Staff may sign in with email and password or with Google.

Clients create a portal password or, if the firm enables it, sign in with Google. That is not a staff account. Guests who book an appointment create a client record in the firm’s workspace.

We may suspend an account that we reasonably believe is used without authorization, in breach of these terms, or in a way that risks the security of the service or other users. The firm remains responsible for activity under its staff accounts.

firmDuties.title: 6. Firm responsibilities and instructions
firmDuties.body:
The firm is responsible for its immigration practice, including retainers, advice, College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (or bar) duties, and privacy obligations toward its clients (including Québec Law 25 and PIPEDA where those apply).

The firm decides what client information to collect and how long to keep it. The firm must obtain valid consent where the law requires it (including express consent for sensitive information), use the product only for lawful professional purposes, configure access so only authorized staff can open files, and complete any privacy impact assessment the law requires of the firm when it adopts this system or communicates information outside Québec.

%OPERATOR_NAME% processes client information as a service provider on the firm’s documented instructions — namely use of the product, the firm’s configuration, the Privacy Policy, and the Firm Data Processing Addendum accepted in-product by a firm administrator. The firm warrants that its instructions are lawful and that it has the authority and consents needed to instruct that processing. %OPERATOR_NAME% may refuse an instruction that would break the law and will inform the firm.

clientUse.title: 7. Client and guest use
clientUse.body:
If you sign in to a firm’s client portal or book through a firm’s page, you are giving information to that firm so it can manage your file or appointment. %OPERATOR_NAME% hosts and processes that information to operate the product. You are not hiring %OPERATOR_NAME%

You must only submit information you are authorized to provide. Do not share a portal password except as the firm instructs. Booking pages are identified by unguessable tokens; do not post them publicly.

Questions about your immigration file, appointment, or the firm’s fees should go to the firm. Optional product analytics are described in the Privacy Policy and are off unless you accept them.

acceptableUse.title: 8. Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body:
You may not:
• Probe, disrupt, or overload the service, or try to bypass security or access controls
• Use another person’s account or portal access without authorization
• Upload malware or content you do not have the right to share
• Use the product to send spam or to mislead IRCC, MIFI, or any government authority
• Resell or sublicense the software except as %OPERATOR_NAME% agrees in writing

We may investigate suspected misuse and cooperate with a firm or with law enforcement where the law requires. We may remove or disable content that we reasonably believe is unlawful or threatens the security of the service.

fees.title: 9. Fees

settings.gstQstHelp: Turn this on when the company is registered. If a GST or QST number is entered, new invoices include tax by default (can be unchecked per invoice). GST and QST each apply to the tax-exclusive amount (rule in force since 2013 — no QST on GST). Enter rates as decimals: 0.05 = 5%, 0.09975 = 9.975%.

settings.fiscalEquityHelp: The opening entry is Dr bank · Cr share capital · Cr retained earnings. The three amounts must balance (cash = capital + retained earnings). Opening cash is the bank balance on that date: if the CSV starts later, it is added to the bank reconciliation balance (not duplicated in the statement). A difference with retained earnings entered goes to suspense account 1190, not 3100. With no retained earnings entered, the cash − capital difference is posted to retained earnings. If opening cash is 0 and the deposit is in the CSV, assign it as “Opening balance (RE)” (this clears 1190). Corporate tax rate: planning decimal (0.205 = 20.5%) — federal 9% SBD + QC 11.5% general, draft for CPA.

periodClose.title: Period close
periodClose.subtitle: Locks an accounting month: payroll, bank, invoices, time, taxes and adjustments — draft for CPA review.

periodClose.wipOff: WIP off — unbilled revenue is not accrued in the books.
periodClose.empty: No closed periods. Close a month once bank reconciliation and payroll are complete.
